assertions.title: Public booking detail and guest booking detail reuse one booking-detail model

steps.expected: Comparison harness shows public and guest booking-detail fixtures side by side for the same cancelled booking state
steps.observed: Harness rendered public and guest booking-detail fixtures side by side with matching cancelled status, The Fox venue, REF NB3456, identical guest info, and the same disabled management affordances.

steps.action: Inspect the exposed recovery continuity targets
steps.expected: Public and guest booking paths should preserve distinct destinations while reusing the same booking-detail model
steps.observed: The harness exposed a Public recovery URL ending in next=%2Fbookings%2F55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555 and a Guest recovery URL ending in next=%2Fguest%2Fbookings%2F55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555, confirming route-appropriate continuity targets from the shared detail model.

evidence.consoleErrors: No console errors attributable to the harness flow; only existing Next/PostHog dev noise and unrelated 404 resource logs appeared after navigation.
evidence.network: Harness loaded successfully on http://localhost:3000/dev/booking-detail-comparison?fixture=cancelled and exposed direct public/guest recovery URLs with real current-runtime tokens.

assertions.title: Recovery flow preserves destination continuity end to end

steps.action: Read the Public recovery URL directly from the comparison harness
steps.expected: The harness should expose a replayable current-runtime recovery URL rather than a placeholder token
steps.observed: The annotated screenshot and DOM text exposed the full /bookings/recover?access_token=sr1...&next=%2Fbookings%2F55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555 URL from the current runtime.

steps.action: Open the exposed Public recovery URL from the comparison harness
steps.expected: Recovery should route through /bookings/recover and land on the intended token-free public booking detail destination without INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN
steps.observed: Following the harness Public recovery URL landed on http://localhost:3000/bookings/55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555 with page title "Booking 55555555 · Nab a Table" and visible cancelled booking detail for The Fox; no INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN screen appeared.

evidence.consoleErrors: No INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN or application exception surfaced while replaying the harness recovery URL; only existing dev console noise remained.
evidence.network: Comparison harness exposed direct recovery URL -> opening that URL resolved to token-free /bookings/55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555.

summary: Fresh comparison-harness replay passed: the current runtime exposes a real public recovery URL and replaying it lands on the token-free public booking detail destination, so both VAL-CROSS-003 and VAL-CROSS-004 now pass.
